sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Early Differential Diagnosis
sections.description: This section reviews the initial patient presentation, early physical findings, imaging, inflammatory markers, and the differential diagnosis that guided the initial workup.
subtopics: Initial symptomatology: progressive neck swelling, proximal hip flexor weakness, mild myalgia
Key physical findings: erythematous facial rash, periungual changes, reduced hip flexor power
Laboratory and imaging at presentation: elevated CRP, normal WBC, CT neck showing diffuse edema of strap muscles
Early differential diagnosis: Ludwig angina, deep neck space infection, idiopathic angioedema

sections.description: This section covers the immunopathogenesis of dermatomyositis, the spectrum of myositis‑specific autoantibodies, with emphasis on the anti‑SAE1 phenotype and its clinical correlates.
subtopics: Dermatomyositis as an immune‑mediated myopathy of skin and muscle
Typical cutaneous manifestations: Gottron papules, heliotrope rash, shawl sign, V‑neck sign
Myositis‑specific antibody spectrum and disease associations
Clinical phenotype of anti‑SAE1 antibody: prominent dysphagia, interstitial lung disease, higher malignancy risk
Pathogenesis of SAE1 autoantibody: SUMO activation, complement deposition in perifascicular capillaries

sections.description: This section outlines the systematic diagnostic approach used in the case, from laboratory panels to advanced imaging and muscle biopsy, and explains how the findings converged on a definitive diagnosis.
subtopics: Comprehensive laboratory workup: CK elevation (16,184 U/L), transaminases, LDH, ANA speckled, myositis antibody panel
Imaging studies: chest CT (ground‑glass opacities, pulmonary nodules), MRI of thighs (perifascicular atrophy), FDG‑PET (diffuse muscle uptake), barium swallow (severe pharyngeal dysphagia)
Muscle biopsy findings: perifascicular necrosis, vacuolated fibres, C5b‑9 deposition
Exclusion of alternative diagnoses: negative cultures, normal complement C3/C4, normal C1‑esterase activity, absence of infectious markers
Diagnostic reasoning to dermatomyositis with anti‑SAE1 positivity

sections.description: This section details the multimodal treatment strategy, including steroid therapy, IVIG, immunosuppressive agents, infection prophylaxis, and supportive airway management, and discusses the rationale behind each component.
subtopics: High‑dose intravenous methylprednisolone induction: 1,000 mg daily for 3 days
IVIG regimen: 2 g/kg over five days, followed by monthly 2 g/kg doses
Steroid‑sparing agents: mycophenolate mofetil 1 g BID, rituximab 1,000 mg IV two weeks apart
Avoidance of methotrexate due to interstitial lung disease risk
Opportunistic infection prophylaxis: TMP‑SMX initially, switched to nebulised pentamidine after haemolytic anaemia
Airway and feeding management: nasogastric tube feeding due to dysphagia, ENT follow‑up

sections.description: This section describes the short‑ and long‑term outcomes, highlights the malignancy surveillance plan per IMACS guidelines, and summarizes key clinical lessons from the case.
subtopics: Early treatment response: CK normalization, improvement in weakness and neck swelling
Long‑term pulmonary recovery: resolution of ground‑glass opacities, persistent mild restrictive pattern
Malignancy risk assessment (IMACS): high‑risk factors – dermatomyositis, dysphagia, anti‑SAE1 positivity, male sex
Surveillance strategy: annual chest CT, abdominal imaging, tumour markers, upper and lower GI endoscopy
Clinical pearls: consider dermatomyositis in unexplained neck swelling; early CK and skin exam are critical; aggressive immunosuppression can lead to remission
